title: Muscle profile
intro: Thinking about the last month, answer 8 short questions with Yes or No. This isn't a diagnosis; it's only used to choose the right programme for you. Your answers stay only on this phone.

questions.text: Do you have ongoing pain or a feeling of pressure in your pelvis, perineum (between the anus and testicles), groin or anus?
Do you have pain that gets worse after sitting for a long time?
Do you have pain during or after ejaculation?
Do you often feel a sudden need to urinate?
Do you feel you can't empty your bladder fully, or have trouble starting to urinate?
Do you have constipation or a need to strain?
Do you find yourself clenching your buttocks or belly without noticing when you're stressed?

questions.note: This can be a sign of muscle weakness; it doesn't count towards the tension score.

result.relaxTitle: We suggest seeing a specialist first
result.relaxText: Your answers suggest your pelvic floor may be holding tension. In that case, squeezing exercises can make discomfort worse. We suggest seeing a urologist or a pelvic floor physiotherapist before you start training.
result.relaxNote: If you feel pain or discomfort during training, stop right away and end the workout. We suggest redoing the screening every 2 weeks.
result.okText: Nothing in your answers clearly points to tension. You can start training.
result.dribbleText: For dribbling after urinating, the habit of “squeeze twice after urinating” can help.
result.painNotice: Stop if it hurts. Kegels should not cause pain; if you feel discomfort, end the workout.
